question_text: What are the functions of Sertoli cells of the seminiferous tubules and the Leydig cells in man?

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.54, VSAQ 102. page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Sertoli cells
steps.why: Developing sperm are cut off from the blood supply, so a nurse cell has to feed them from inside the tubule.
common_mistakes: Giving Sertoli cells the testosterone job. Leydig cells make it.
steps.memory_tip: Sertoli cells are the nurse cells; inhibin is their hormone.
lines: Sertoli cells are nourishing cells. They
They also produce a hormone called inhibin,
which stops the production of FSH.

steps.label: Leydig cells
steps.why: The hormone must reach the whole body, so it is made outside the tubules where the blood vessels run.
common_mistakes: Placing Leydig cells inside the tubules. They lie between them.
steps.memory_tip: Leydig cells lie between the tubules and make testosterone.
steps.margin_note: Say where they are and what they make.
lines: Leydig cells are interstitial cells between

insider_note: Two cells, one mark each. Sertoli cells also make inhibin — that extra fact is what lifts the answer from a bare naming.
